context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Deuteronomy 21:1–9.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: An unresolved murder leads to elders, sacrifice, washing, confession of nonparticipation, a request for forgiveness.
observations.label: An unresolved murder leads to a pardon request: action
An unresolved murder leads to a pardon request: response

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 21:1–9 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: An unresolved murder leads to elders, sacrifice, washing, confession of nonparticipation, a request for forgiveness, and removal of innocent blood.
payload.title: An unresolved murder leads to a pardon request
